observed: Used an isolated Playwright Chrome 154 context (375x812, DPR 2, Android UA, touch, mobile emulation) because the shared Browser-pane tabs were occupied and a new tab could not be created. Step 1: opened http://localhost:4180/ at 375 wide; before the hack innerWidth 375, scrollWidth 375, no overflow. Step 2: ran the exact hack (html font-size 200%, body zoom 2). In the mobile preset innerWidth jumped from 375 to 589 and scrollWidth was 589, so the literal 'scrollWidth <= innerWidth' reads equal only because the emulation inflated innerWidth; documentElement.clientWidth stayed 375 and a touch swipe-left panned the page 214px sideways (visualViewport.pageLeft 0 -> 214). In a plain 375px viewport (innerWidth stays 375) scrollWidth is 589, 214px over, and window.scrollX reaches 214. With genuine 200% browser zoom (188px viewport, no hack, supplemental) scrollWidth is 291 vs innerWidth 188. Element scan: 89 element boxes past the screen edge all sit inside their own overflow-x:auto containers (header nav, install tab strip, install command pre, criteria table wrapper, models table wrapper), each of which fits the screen. But 3 elements are not contained: the footer nav (GitHub, Issues, Discussions, Security; display flex, flex-wrap nowrap, overflow visible) is 549px wide in a 311px footer and ends at x=581 (links Discussions and Security past the edge). Text also pokes past the edge outside any scroller: p.computed (long unbreakable timestamp and tree hashes, right edge 472.7) and, under the hack only, the h1 word 'definition' (right edge 589.5). With true 200% zoom the footer nav and p.computed still overflow (right 290.6 and 236.3 vs 188); the h1 fits. Step 3: scrolled the install block: all four tabs' command blocks (440/120, 389/120, 288/120, 431/120, 876/120 scrollWidth/clientWidth) scroll inside their own block by mouse wheel, the text end becomes visible (end edge ~279-281 <= block edge 307) and the page does not move. Criteria table (399/156) and Models table (371/156) scroll inside their own wrapper and every row's last cell is reachable. No overflow:hidden/clip or ellipsis clipping anywhere and nothing left of x=0. The footer links and the overflowing p.computed text are reachable only by scrolling the whole page sideways, which is the failure itself. Step 4: closed the mobile contexts; a fresh 1280x800 desktop context loads at innerWidth 1280, scrollWidth 1280 with no zoom or font-size set.
expected: At 375 wide with font-size 200% and body zoom 2: scrollWidth does not exceed innerWidth (no horizontal page scroll); any element wider than the viewport is a command or table container that scrolls inside itself, not the page; no text clipped without a way to scroll to it.
notes: FAIL on expectations 1 and 2, expectation 3 held with a caveat. Root cause is the footer nav: a nowrap flex row with no overflow rule inside a wrapping footer; also p.computed has unbreakable tokens. Measurement caveat: in Chrome mobile emulation innerWidth grows to match overflowing content (375 -> 589), so compare scrollWidth with documentElement.clientWidth (375) or run at non-mobile 375 (innerWidth stays 375, scrollWidth 589). html font-size 200% alone does not overflow (375/375/375); body zoom 2 alone does (scrollWidth 581). The hack compounds on rem-sized text (h1 computed 64px vs 32px), so it is harsher than real zoom, but real 200% zoom (188px viewport) still overflows through the footer nav and p.computed. Console had only Vite debug lines and the React DevTools info message; no errors, no failed requests (Google Fonts loaded). Other: at 200% the sticky header takes about 215 of 812px (26%) and overlaps content; the criteria table wrapper is about 5,850px tall because the outcome column wraps in a narrow cell. Evidence summary per expectation: 00-summary-per-expectation.txt.
